named_public_import_and_prior_art: Sang-Jun Park, k-Positivity and high-dimensional bound entanglement under symplectic group symmetry, arXiv:2602.09860v1, https://arxiv.org/html/2602.09860v1, especially Theorem 1.2. This public source identifies the generalized Breuer-Hall maps used below. The positivity, PPT-pairing, and input-compression decomposability claims below are independently reconstructed in written algebra; nevertheless prior art and novelty of the compression statement are not established. This is post-contact work. No Johnston-Lovitz article or held episode is used in the proof.
main_result: For every even d and integer k with 1<=k<d/2, let J be a dxd skew-symmetric unitary, j=vec(J), F the swap, W_(k,d)=k I_(d^2)-kF-[j], and R_d=I_(d^2)+F+[j]. Then R_d is PPT, W_(k,d) is k-block positive, and Tr(W_(k,d) R_d)=d(2k-d)<0. However, for every local filter A of rank at most 2k, every local filter B of any rank, and every PPT state sigma on C^d tensor C^d, Tr[W_(k,d)(A tensor B)sigma(A tensor B)^*]>=0. In particular the explicit NEW pair d=6,k=2 has Tr(W R)=-12, but no rank<=4 Alice filter and no Bob filter, including rank<=4, yields a negative pairing. This limitation is of this specific symplectic witness family, NOT of all witnesses, all new source pairs, or the 4x4 target.
source_pair_and_positivity: For the concrete pair choose real J=[[0,I_3],[-I_3,0]], so J^T=-J and J^T J=I_6; j=vec(J) has squared norm d and Fj=-j. For general complex skew-unitary J, R=I+F+[j] is PSD since I+F=2P_sym, and its Bob partial transpose is I+[Omega]+(I tensor conjugate(J))F(I tensor conjugate(J)^*), where Omega=sum_i |ii>. The twisted swap is a Hermitian involution, so I plus it is PSD. In the concrete real case conjugate(J)=J and conjugate(J)^*=J^T. R has trace d(d+2). Since Tr(FR)=d^2 and <j|R|j>=d^2, Tr(W_(k,d)R)=k d(d+2)-k d^2-d^2=d(2k-d), equal to -12 for d=6,k=2. For any coefficient matrix Y of rank <=k, let S=(Y-Y^T)/2; rank(S)<=2k and <j|Y>=Tr(J^*S). The trace-norm inequality gives |Tr(J^*S)|^2 <= ||S||_*^2 <= 2k ||S||_F^2, and <Y|W_(k,d)|Y>=2k||S||_F^2-|Tr(J^*S)|^2>=0. Thus the witness is k-block positive and the negative PPT pairing makes it indecomposable. Park's normalized map is a positive scalar multiple after a fixed local unitary on Bob.
canonical_compression: It suffices to restrict the first subsystem to any 2k-dimensional isometry U, because every smaller-rank filter factors through such a U and decomposability is preserved under completely positive pre/post-composition. Write E=ran(U), select an orthonormal complement U_perp, and put K=U^* J conjugate(U), N=U^* J conjugate(U_perp). K is complex skew-symmetric, KK^*+NN^*=I_(2k), and its singular values are paired. The standard unitary congruence normal form of a complex skew-symmetric matrix gives K=direct_sum_i lambda_i [[0,1],[-1,0]], with 0<=lambda_i<=1. Set s_i=sqrt(1-lambda_i^2). The nonzero rows of NN^*=direct_sum_i s_i^2 I_2 are orthogonal pairs, so after a unitary choice of complement coordinates each defective pair s_i>0 has its own two outside output coordinates p_i,q_i. In these bases the compressed vector j_U=(U^* tensor I)j is sum_i lambda_i a_i + sum_(s_i>0) s_i c_i, where a_i=|2i-1,2i>-|2i,2i-1> and c_i=|2i-1,p_i>-|2i,q_i>. The a_i and c_i are mutually orthogonal, each has squared norm 2, and sum_i lambda_i^2+sum_(s_i>0)s_i^2=k. The compressed swap is the ordinary swap F_E on C^(2k) tensor E, extended by zero outside E. Thus C_U=(U^* tensor I)W_(k,d)(U tensor I)=k I-k F_E-[j_U].
explicit_decomposition: For each defective i put h_i=|2i-1,q_i>+|2i,p_i>. Let u_alpha list all a_i and the c_i for defective pairs, and let w_alpha list the corresponding real lambda_i and s_i. Let A_other contain all unnormalized antisymmetric vectors |p,q>-|q,p> with p<q<=2k except the k paired vectors a_i. Let B_other contain the standard basis vectors |p,o> with p an input coordinate and o an output-complement coordinate, excluding the 2x2 input/output block of each defective pair. Then the following equality is an explicit decomposable Choi representation, with Gamma on the input factor: C_U=P+k sum_(s_i>0)[h_i]^Gamma, where P=sum_(alpha<beta)[w_alpha u_beta-w_beta u_alpha]+k sum_(v in A_other)[v]+k sum_(v in B_other)[v] >=0. To see this directly, kI-kF_E is 2k on the antisymmetric E sector, 0 on the symmetric E sector, and k on the outside sector. Each [h_i]^Gamma acts as -1 on c_i, +1 on its symmetric companion and on the two cross basis vectors in its 2x2 block, and 0 elsewhere. Removing k sum [h_i]^Gamma therefore makes the diagonal coefficient on every normalized u_alpha equal to 2k and kills the other three modes per defective block. On their span, [j_U] has coefficient matrix 2ww^T and w^Tw=k; the displayed sum of outer products is exactly 2(k I-ww^T). The remaining antisymmetric and outside modes give the two other PSD sums. Thus P and sum [h_i] are explicitly PSD for all variables, with no search or sampled-parameter assumption.
filter_consequence: Let rank(A)<=2k and factor A=U C with U an isometry with 2k columns. Congruencing the decomposition by C on the input preserves decomposability (the partial-transposed positive summand is congruenced by conjugate(C)). Congruencing by arbitrary B on the output also preserves it. Every PPT sigma pairs nonnegatively with a decomposable operator, proving the full filter statement. Choosing sigma=R_d specializes it to the new explicit source pair. Neither the decomposition nor its consequence asserts anything about 4x4 states or witnesses outside this family.
exact_arithmetic_evidence: On this post-contact turn, frontier-20261029-symplectic-rank4-decomposition-check.py SHA256 3bc5a9fed2acbb676c001622de579b559b87ab3058827247d0a13fcf9aeaa115 was executed inside the Python eval kernel. Using integer polynomial arithmetic, it checked all 576 entries of the d=6,k=2 canonical decomposition modulo s^2+lambda^2=1, and verified trace(R_6)=48, Tr(W_2,6 R_6)=-12, the partial-transpose formula and twisted-swap involution exactly. Independently, frontier-20261029-symplectic-d8-two-defect-check.py SHA256 1d15ac6d082990fde8436077ea73f808a888643c7f75872e9bcf413cac42331f checked all 1024 entries for d=8,k=2 with two independently variable defective pairs, modulo both quadratic identities. General k,d is supported by the explicit written basis/SOS proof above, not by these two finite checks; neither is a proof-assistant verification.
